title: Lower-bound characterisation of public-coin complexity
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, and let $m \in \bbn$. Write $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f)$ for the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$, namely the infimum in $\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$ of the worst-case bit complexity over all public-coin protocols that compute $f$ with error at most $\varepsilon$ on every input. Then $m \le \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f)$ if and only if, for every $n \in \bbn$ and every public-coin protocol $p$ using a coin tape of length $n$, whenever $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ its communication complexity satisfies $m \le \mathrm{complexity}(p)$.
hypotheses_covered: quantification over all tape lengths n
quantification over all public-coin protocols p on CoinTape(n)
the hypothesis that p ε-computes f
